These checks validate the diagnostics mechanism without reproducing a flight failure. Native DLL versions are checked against their source declarations.

Windows releases consume that workflow's artifact. Both PyInstaller packaging and the final packaged directory must pass verification; old checked-in DLLs cannot silently substitute for the compiled artifact. Native binaries retain debug information and are excluded from UPX so their recorded hashes survive packaging. Keep the matching windows-native CI artifact for native analysis.

The separate Windows diagnostic build workflow produces a portable AutoOrtho_windows_native_diagnostics.zip artifact after native Windows checks pass. It runs for relevant pull requests and can also be started manually. This is a build artifact, without creating a GitHub release.

For a local cross-build with a MinGW POSIX toolchain installed:

make -B -C autoortho/aopipeline -f Makefile.mingw64 windows-bundle \
  CC=x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc-posix LD=x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc-posix
python autoortho/native_build.py record --source-root . \
  --directory autoortho/aopipeline/lib/windows --revision <commit-id>
python autoortho/native_build.py verify --source-root . \
  --directory autoortho/aopipeline/lib/windows

Frozen workers also verify the bundled artifact hashes before native imports. An unmanifested development checkout logs that it is unverified; a frozen build rejects missing or mismatched native artifacts.

docs.title: Plan: detecting "behind the aircraft" from prefetch misses
docs.text: Status: implemented (steps 1-5); thresholds are the starting values below until flight reports set them. See the proposal's implementation notes for where the code differs from this plan. Related: settings-refactor-proposal.md §4.4 (the Behind the aircraft row of the bottleneck classifier) and its phases 5-6 notes

docs.title: 1. Problem
docs.text:
The governor's behind state is a fallback today. Governor.classify() returns it when fewer than 95 % of near reads are sharp and nothing else explains it: the network is not saturated, the CPU is not the limit, and the late-arrival evidence (wait_evidence()) does not ask for a longer wait. In that state the governor lengthens prefetch lookahead and widens the radius.

That move is a guess. Your proposal's §4.4 defines the state by evidence ("near reads hit tiles that prefetch never queued, line and CPU have room"), but nothing records which tiles prefetch queued. So the governor can't tell apart four cases that need different fixes:

What happened to the tile X-Plane read blurry Real cause Right move No prefetch path ever queued it The corridor was too short or too narrow, or prefetch was paused Longer lookahead or a wider radius, or find the pause It was queued, but not finished when X-Plane read it Prefetch started too late, or had too little capacity A longer paging lead, or the existing network/compute rules It was queued only to a coarser level than X-Plane wanted The paging model under-estimated the detail A longer paging lead, or report a k mismatch It was finished, then dropped from memory before the read Memory cache too small A bigger memory cache, if RAM allows

Widening prefetch only helps in the first case. In the other three it adds downloads that compete with X-Plane's own reads.

docs.title: 2. Goal
docs.text:
• Classify every blurry near read in flight by what prefetch had done for that tile beforehand.
  • Base the behind state on that classification, and give each cause its own move.
  • Without evidence, move nothing: today's blind prefetch increase goes away.
  • Ship the measurement and the flight-report table first, with no governor rule, so the thresholds come from real flights (as Advise did).

Out of scope: changing how the prefetcher chooses tiles. This plan only measures and tunes the existing knobs.

docs.title: 3. Where prefetch queues tiles today
docs.text:
Every path ends in one of two places, so two hooks cover them all:

Path Code Ends in Velocity corridor SpatialPrefetcher._do_velocity_prefetch_cycle() _prefetch_tile() SimBrief route / waypoints _prefetch_along_flight_plan*(), _prefetch_waypoint_area() _prefetch_tile() Paging warm (coarse levels) SpatialPrefetcher.paging_split() _prefetch_tile(first_mip=…) .ter load-ahead load_ahead_warm() _prefetch_tile(first_mip=…) DSF prefetch, paging-coarse tiles prefetch_dsf() (the camera branch) _prefetch_tile(first_mip=…) DSF prefetch, corridor tiles prefetch_dsf() PrefetchCoordinator.publish() prefetch_tiles() fallback SpatialPrefetcher.prefetch_tiles() _prefetch_tile()

When a tile is done:

  • PrefetchCoordinator._finish_candidate(candidate, CandidateState.COMPLETE) (prefetch.py)
  • BackgroundDDSBuilder storing a predictive DDS (dynamic_dds_cache.store)
  • the chunks queued by _prefetch_tile() arriving: TileCompletionTracker already watches these for predictive DDS

When a tile leaves memory: TileCacher eviction (it already records _recently_evicted[idx] = now, getortho.py near line 17952).

When X-Plane reads a tile blurry: Tile._read_dds_bytes_budgeted(), in the branch that bumps near_reads_standin (getortho.py).

docs.title: 4.1 Prefetch ledger (per worker process)
docs.text:
Each mount worker runs its own prefetcher and serves its own reads, so the ledger stays in the worker and no cross-process channel is needed.

New module autoortho/prefetch_ledger.py. It must be pure: no getortho import, and the clock is injected, so tests run without a tile cacher.

@dataclass
class LedgerEntry:
    first_queued: float            # monotonic time of the first queue
    finest_mip: int                # finest level any path queued (0 = full)
    sources: frozenset[str]        # "velocity", "simbrief", "paging", "ter", "dsf"
    done_at: Optional[float] = None
    done_mip: Optional[int] = None # finest level known complete
    evicted_at: Optional[float] = None

class PrefetchLedger:
    MAX_ENTRIES = 8192             # ~100 B each: under 1 MB
    TTL_S = 1200.0                 # 20 min, as the graphics memory meter

    def note_queued(self, key, mip, source, now): ...
    def note_done(self, key, mip, now): ...
    def note_evicted(self, key, now): ...
    def classify_miss(self, key, wanted_mip, now) -> str: ...
  • Key: (row, col, zoom), without the maptype. DSF prefetch may rewrite the maptype (maptype_override) while reads use the resolved one, so a key that includes it would split one tile into two entries. Different maptypes for one tile in one session are rare, and merging them only makes a miss look covered.
  • Bounded: an OrderedDict used as an LRU, with entries older than TTL_S dropped on access. One lock, held only for dictionary work.
  • note_queued keeps the finest mip and the earliest time, and adds the source.
  • note_done sets done_at and done_mip; note_evicted sets evicted_at.

classify_miss(key, wanted_mip, now) returns, checking in this order:

  1. "never": no entry, or the first queue was less than MIN_LEAD_S (2 s) before the read. A queue that came that late is a reaction to X-Plane, not foresight.
  2. "evicted": done_mip <= wanted_mip and evicted_at > done_at.
  3. "coarse": finest_mip > wanted_mip (only a coarser level was queued).
  4. "late": queued at finest_mip <= wanted_mip, but not done (done_at is None or done_mip > wanted_mip).
  5. "done": complete at the wanted level and not evicted. The read was blurry for another reason (a failed chunk, or a level marked as missing colour). Counted, not acted on.

docs.title: 4.2 Hooks
docs.text:
All hooks are best effort: wrapped in try/except and logged at debug level, like _note_wanted_level().

Hook Call SpatialPrefetcher._prefetch_tile(), after it submitted at least one chunk or found the tile complete ledger.note_queued((row, col, zoom), first_mip, source, now). source is a new keyword argument, passed by each caller from the table in §3 (default "velocity"). prefetch_dsf(), after prefetch_coordinator.publish() returned created or the key was already known ledger.note_queued(key, 0, "dsf", now) PrefetchCoordinator._finish_candidate(…, COMPLETE) a new optional on_complete(key) callback set by getortho, which calls ledger.note_done(key, 0, now) TileCompletionTracker, when all of a tile's queued chunks are ready ledger.note_done(key, first_mip_of_that_submission, now) TileCacher eviction (_recently_evicted[idx] = now) ledger.note_evicted(key, now) Tile._read_dds_bytes_budgeted(), near band, not real, not starting, X-Plane connected kind = ledger.classify_miss(key, wanted, now), then bump(f"near_miss_{kind}")

Geometry for "never" misses. A tile prefetch never queued either lay outside the corridor (fix: radius) or inside it while prefetch did not run (fix: find the pause). To tell which, the read hook also computes the tile's cross-track offset from the aircraft track at the time of the read, using current_camera() and paging_model.bearing_deg() / ground_distance_m(), which already exist:

  • |cross_track| > 0.8 × prefetch_radius → near_miss_never_wide
  • otherwise → near_miss_never_inside

never_inside while prefetch was paused points at the pauses: the RAM brake (ram_brake_activations), live pressure (LivePressureController), prefetch_during_live_reads = False, or the runtime gate (is_prefetch_runtime_allowed()). Also bump near_miss_never_paused when any of these was active in the last prefetch_interval seconds. SpatialPrefetcher records the time of its last skipped cycle as self._last_skip_at.

Turns. In a turn, tiles on the outside of the turn are never in a straight-ahead corridor. The read hook runs in the worker, so the ledger keeps its own small deque of (time, track_deg) from current_camera() (its fourth field), appended at most once a second. When the track changed by more than 30° in the last 60 s, count the miss as near_miss_never_turn instead of wide. A wider radius is the wrong fix for a turn; SimBrief prefetch already covers planned turns.

docs.title: 4.3 Governor
docs.text:
New Sample fields (cumulative counters, all workers summed, read like near_reads_standin):

near_miss_never_wide, near_miss_never_inside, near_miss_never_paused,
near_miss_never_turn, near_miss_coarse, near_miss_late,
near_miss_evicted, near_miss_done

Window gets their deltas over the 30 s window.

Classification replaces today's return "behind" fallback. It runs only when fidelity is under FIDELITY_LOW and wait_evidence() did not return "wait" or "too_slow":

misses = w.miss_counts            # dict kind -> count in the window
total = sum(misses.values())
if total < MIN_MISSES:            # 10 in 30 s
    return "ok"                   # no evidence: move nothing
kind, count = max(misses.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1])
if count < 0.5 * total:
    return "ok"                   # no single cause
return {
    "never_wide": "behind_wide",
    "never_inside": "behind_short",
    "never_paused": "prefetch_paused",
    "never_turn": "ok",           # turns: nothing to tune
    "coarse": "paging_coarse",
    "late": "prefetch_late",
    "evicted": "memory_evicted",
    "done": "ok",
}[kind]

Moves (_PLAN):

State Move Note behind_wide prefetch_radius_nm +1 step behind_short prefetch_lookahead +1 step Inside the corridor yet never queued: usually the corridor ended too early for the speed prefetch_paused none Notice naming the pause ("prefetch paused by low memory 40 % of the last 5 minutes"). The RAM brake is the right owner. paging_coarse new lever streaming.paging_lead_seconds +1 step Already read at call time through streaming_options, so it is live with no engine change. Range 30-180 s, step 15 s. prefetch_late streaming.paging_lead_seconds +1, then autoortho.prefetch_max_chunks +1 Starts prefetch earlier first, then lets it do more per cycle. Skipped when the network is saturated (already a network state). memory_evicted cache.cache_mem_limit +1 Only when not in the memory state and RSS is under 80 % of ram_gb

Keep/revert metric for these states: the share of near misses of that kind (lower is better). _metric() returns -share for them.

Headroom easing (state == "headroom") already brings prefetch_lookahead, prefetch_radius_nm and the new lever back toward baseline, so no new decay code is needed.

levers_for() gains:

LeverSpec("streaming.paging_lead_seconds", "Prefetch lead time",
          15, 30, 180, unit="s", group="prefetch"),
LeverSpec("autoortho.prefetch_max_chunks", "Prefetch chunks per cycle",
          64, 128, 2048, group="prefetch"),

Both are already handled live: prefetch_max_chunks has a live_settings hook (_on_live_prefetch), and paging_lead_seconds is read at call time. Add paging_lead_seconds to the registry with owner="governed", live=True.

STATE_TEXT and the unreachable notice's "limiting" map gain the new states in plain words: "Prefetch corridor too narrow", "Prefetch starts too late", "Prefetch asks for too little detail", "Prefetch paused", "Memory cache too small". home_snapshot.BOTTLENECK_GAUGE maps memory_evicted to computer and the others to no gauge, since they are prefetch rather than a resource.

docs.title: 4.4 Transparency
docs.text:
• Flight report (diagnostics._render_flight): a Blurry moments by cause table with the share of each miss kind, by phase. It ships in step 1, before any governor rule.
  • Tuning page: the decision reason gives the evidence, for example "prefetch corridor too narrow: 14 of 18 blurry tiles lay 6-9 nm off the track".
  • Home: no new block. A prefetch_paused notice reaches Home only when it repeats (§13.5: raw counters stay off Home).

docs.title: 5. Work plan
docs.text:
Each step can ship on its own.

Step Content Files Tests 1. Ledger PrefetchLedger, LedgerEntry, classify_miss() new prefetch_ledger.py new tests/test_prefetch_ledger.py: queue → read (never / late / coarse / done), done → evict → read (evicted), finest-mip merge, the LRU bound, TTL expiry, MIN_LEAD_S 2. Hooks the source argument on _prefetch_tile() and its callers; DSF publish; coordinator on_complete; completion tracker; eviction; read-side classify_miss + geometry + turn + pause tagging getortho.py, prefetch.py extend tests/test_paging_prefetch.py and tests/test_load_ahead.py (each path records its source and mip); a tile read test like test_late_arrivals.py::test_tile_watches_… for the miss counters; coordinator test for on_complete 3. Report Blurry moments by cause in the flight report; counters in the timeline JSON diagnostics.py, governor.py (summary) tests/test_tuning_ui.py::test_report_renders_flight_verdict extended — Fly 5-10 flights with step 3, read the reports, set MIN_MISSES, the 50 % dominance share and the 0.8 × radius threshold from them 4. Governor rules Sample/Window fields; new states and moves; paging_lead_seconds and prefetch_max_chunks levers; _metric for the new states; remove the blind behind fallback governor.py, settings_registry.py, aoconfig.py (template comment), home_snapshot.py tests/test_governor.py: one classifier case per kind, no move without evidence, keep/revert on the miss share, and a replay test over a recorded samples-*.jsonl from step 3 5. Docs docs/config.md governor section; proposal implementation notes docs —

Rough size: step 1 about 150 lines plus tests. Step 2 is the risky one, since _prefetch_tile() has seven callers; about 120 lines. Step 4 is about 120 lines in governor.py.

docs.title: 6. Risks and decisions
docs.text:
• The starting phase. While X-Plane loads an area, every near read is a "never" miss, because prefetch can't know where a flight starts. Starting is excluded with the same flight_is_starting() the wait bands use, plus the jump rule in wait_bands.StartTracker.
  • Teleports and replays. Same as starting: the jump detection covers them.
  • Lock contention. note_queued runs once per tile submission (at most a few hundred per prefetch cycle), and classify_miss once per blurry near read. One dictionary lookup under a lock: negligible next to the chunk work around it.
  • Key mismatch between prefetch and reads. Prefetch uses the .ter zoom (zoom in _prefetch_tile(row, col, zoom)), and reads use tilename_zoom. Both are the file's zoom, but step 2's tests must assert that one tile gives the same key on both sides, including a DSF tile with maptype_override.
  • Several workers. Each worker's ledger sees only its own prefetches and reads. A tile belongs to one scenery package, so to one worker. The governor sums the counters, as it already does for near_reads_*.
  • Paging k. paging_coarse often means k is wrong rather than the lead too short. Once the fitted k is persisted (the deferred "keep the measured paging k" item), a coarse miss share that stays high after the lead reached its maximum should become a notice suggesting a k check.
  • Behaviour change. Removing the blind behind fallback means a low fidelity with no evidence moves nothing. That is intended, but _note_limited() only runs for states with moves, so the unreachable notice would no longer fire in that case. Add a separate state, unexplained, for fidelity under FIDELITY_LOW with no dominant miss cause. It has no moves; after UNREACHABLE_AFTER_S it sets the notice "Scenery was often blurry and AutoOrtho could not tell why; the flight report lists the blurry tiles by cause". The classifier above returns unexplained instead of ok in its two "no evidence" branches whenever fidelity is low.

docs.title: 7. Done when
docs.text:
• The flight report shows blurry near reads by cause for every flight.
  • The governor's behind_*, paging_coarse, prefetch_late and memory_evicted decisions cite the miss evidence in their reason, and replay tests over recorded flights reproduce them.
  • No prefetch lever moves without at least MIN_MISSES classified misses in the window.

docs.title: Resource usage: design
docs.text: Date: 2026-11-15. Status: implemented on fix/3.1.0-bugs.

docs.title: Why
docs.text:
AutoOrtho's RAM and CPU go mostly to its own design, not to Python. OrthoStudio XP Live (also Python) used 0.32 cores and 2.9 GB in flight against 0.57 cores and 3.8 GB for AutoOrtho in OrthoStudio's own comparison. OrthoStreamXP (C#) is still a virtual file system but serves finished textures as plain files. Three things cost AutoOrtho the most:

  1. Every texture X-Plane opens lives in AutoOrtho's RAM. A disk-cache hit reads the whole DDS (11 MB BC1, 22 MB BC3 at 4096 px), decompresses it (zstd) and copies it into a Tile. Tiles stay until RSS-driven eviction removes them.
  2. One Python process per scenery mount, each with its own interpreter, thread pools, prefetcher, tile cache and memory limit, coordinated through a shared stat that can go stale.
  3. Live admission counts builds, not bytes. Sixteen mipmap-0 builds and sixteen 256 px builds cost the same "slot", so the gate is either too loose (a burst of mm0 builds) or too tight (many far reads).

Measured on cached imagery (Apple, ZL16/17, ISPC BC1, 4096 px): zstd level 3 saves 9-13 % of a DDS (not the 30-60 % the old config comment claimed), costs ~40 ms of CPU per store and ~9 ms per load, and forces the whole file through RAM.

docs.title: 1. Finished textures served from disk ("direct reads")
docs.text:
[pydds] serve_from_disk = True (default).

  • Open. Before creating a Tile, autoortho_fuse.open() asks getortho.open_disk_texture() for the texture. It answers with a DiskTexture only when the DDS cache holds an entry that is: at the tile's current target zoom, not stale (format, compressor), uncompressed on disk, complete and exact in mipmap 0 (every row real target imagery, nothing missing or fallback), every level populated, and exactly the expected size. Otherwise the live Tile path runs as before. A texture X-Plane already has open as a live Tile stays on that path so one texture is never served two ways.
  • Read. Positional reads from one shared file handle per cache file. Mipmap-0 rows are checked against their SHA-256 row manifest the first time each row is read (once per file per process); later levels have no manifest and are trusted (atomic writes). The season colour table is applied exactly as the live path does. Each read is still classified (read_pattern.classify) so the paging model and the held-texture statistics keep their samples.
  • Fallback. A short read, I/O error or checksum mismatch invalidates the cache entry and switches that handle to a live Tile for the rest of its reads. X-Plane never sees an error.
  • Pins. Entries open for direct reads are skipped by LRU eviction (on Windows the delete would fail and orphan the file; on POSIX it would waste the work).
  • Storage. With direct reads on, new entries are written uncompressed. A compressed entry that is otherwise servable is rewritten uncompressed in the background on its first hit, so the next open is direct.
  • Dropping RAM copies. A live Tile that X-Plane has closed and whose DDS is on disk is dropped by the cleaner on its next pass instead of waiting for memory pressure: every later open is a direct read.

The OS file cache now holds hot textures: shared, reclaimed under pressure, not charged to AutoOrtho.

docs.title: 2. One process for every mount
docs.text:
[fuse] shared_worker = True (Windows and Linux only). macOS always keeps one worker per mount: that was the reason for per-mount workers in the first place, since macFUSE cannot run several mounts from one process through the Python FUSE binding. The setting is ignored there, and the worker itself refuses a multi-mount launch on macOS.

The parent starts one mount worker with every scenery (--mount root|mountpoint|volname repeated). The worker runs each FUSE loop on its own thread and shares one TileCacher (one memory limit, one prefetcher, one DDS builder, one download pool). The worker CPU share (AO_MOUNT_WORKER_COUNT, OpenMP budget) becomes 1, so native code gets the whole CPU budget instead of 1/N each. The parent keeps one handle per mount so status, unmount and restart code is unchanged; all handles of a shared worker share its process.

Crash isolation is not lost in practice: X-Plane crashes when any mount it is reading disappears, so a dead worker per mount never kept a flight alive.

docs.title: 3. Memory-weighted live admission
docs.text:
_live_tile_admission becomes a WeightedGate: the governor's count limit stays, and a byte budget is added ([autoortho] live_build_memory_mb, default derived from cache_mem_limit: 1/4, between 256 MB and 2 GB). Each read is weighted by the working set of the level it builds (RGBA + BC data, about size² × 4.5 bytes: 75 MB at 4096 px, 1.2 MB at 512 px). A request heavier than the whole budget is admitted when nothing else holds the gate, so nothing starves.

Buffer pooling already exists (DDSBufferPool, StreamingBuilderPool), so no new pool is added.

Direct reads need the DDS cache, so they are off when predictive DDS (or spatial prefetch, which feeds it) is disabled.

docs.title: 4. Startup downloads
docs.text: Audited, not changed. OrthoStudio's comparison ran upstream AutoOrtho. This branch already has the OrthoStreamXP techniques that cut start-up downloads, all on by default (streaming_options.DEFAULTS): the read classifier (header chunks served from one base chunk), the low-zoom base, paging prefetch (DSF prefetch fetches only the level X-Plane will want), terrain load-ahead and wait bands. Any further trimming needs a measured flight (the dsf_paging_coarse_chunks, read_header_chunks and download byte counters) rather than a guess.

docs.title: Not done
docs.text: Building textures ahead to plain files with no virtual file system (OrthoStudio Live's model): deliberately out of scope (delicate, and heavy on disk writes).

docs.title: Settings refactor proposal: Target, Limits, Governor
docs.text: Status: phases 1 to 9 implemented (see "Implementation notes" at the end); the governor ships in Auto mode, starting from the tuning plan (see "Tuner completion" at the end) Scope: user-facing settings, how settings are stored and resolved, the setup wizard, and a live auto-tuning engine Reference studied: OrthoStreamXP (OSXP), shared with permission. This proposal borrows its measurement ideas but keeps AutoOrtho's own model.

docs.title: 1. Summary
docs.text:
AutoOrtho asks beginners to set about 89 controls across 148 config keys. Most of those controls set how the engine works (workers, budgets, buffers, broker limits) rather than what the user wants. Users copy values from forum posts that were tuned for someone else's PC, overload their machine, and blame AutoOrtho.

This proposal splits settings into three things the user can reason about, plus one thing the user never has to set:

Who owns it What it is Target User What I want to see. An imagery zoom level, either fixed or by altitude (the existing dynamic zoom steps), with a separate airport zoom. Limits User (auto by default) What I allow AutoOrtho to use. RAM, graphics memory, download bandwidth, CPU share, disk. Detected automatically; the user can lower any of them. Guards AutoOrtho Protection. RAM/VRAM/disk/bandwidth checks before a flight and emergency brakes during it. They warn and offer a fix, but never block. Governor AutoOrtho How to get there. A background control loop that adjusts every engine setting live, during the flight, to deliver the target as closely and as quickly as the machine, the network and the limits allow. It remembers what worked for next time.

What makes this AutoOrtho's own rather than a copy of OSXP:

  • The user keeps the zoom-level vocabulary and the altitude-based profiles that experienced users value. They are not replaced by named presets.
  • Tuning is continuous, not post-flight. OSXP suggests one change after each flight and waits for the user's OK. AutoOrtho adjusts within seconds, during the flight, inside limits the user set. An Advise mode keeps the OSXP-style "suggest, you apply" behaviour for users who prefer it.
  • Everything the governor does is visible. A live panel shows target vs delivered quality, the current bottleneck, every adjusted value, its allowed range, and the reason for its last change. Any value can be pinned so the governor leaves it alone.
  • Resource limits are a first-class setting. The user can say "never use more than 8 GB RAM or 100 Mbit/s", and the governor treats that as a hard ceiling.
  • A new Home page (§13) shows it all working: quality delivered against the target, resource use against limits, what AutoOrtho is doing ahead of the aircraft, and what the tuner changed. The layout changes with the state (stopped, loading, flying, after flight) and keeps engine internals off the page.

docs.title: 2. What we take from OSXP, and what we do differently
docs.text: OSXP idea AutoOrtho adopts? AutoOrtho version One quality knob (level-change) that hides zoom levels No The user picks a target zoom level (fixed or altitude profile). Presets are only shortcuts that fill in the target. Presets carry every hidden setting Partly Hidden settings come from the hardware baseline and the governor's learned profile, not from fixed preset tables. Connection test (rounds of 16 to 256 parallel downloads, 30 s) Yes Used as the governor's warm start on first run and as a feasibility check in the wizard. VRAM detection from the driver registry Yes, extended Windows registry as OSXP, plus Linux/macOS sources. Feeds the guards. Graphics memory measured per texture size from flights Yes Feeds the VRAM guard and the target cost preview. Paging model with k measured in flight Already ported (paging_model.py) The governor stores the fitted k so each flight starts from it. Post-flight tuner: one step per flight, opt-in Changed Becomes the slow loop of the governor (cross-flight learning). Live tuning handles the rest. Opt-in behaviour remains as Advise mode. Per-preset tuned store, Reset Yes, generalised Learned profiles are stored per (target profile, imagery provider, network), with Reset. Cap texture size at 4096 px and shrink finer imagery Optional lever Off by default because it changes what the user asked for. If the user allows it, the governor can use it to fit VRAM limits without lowering the zoom level. No altitude settings No Dynamic zoom steps stay. They now also get a cost preview and VRAM checks. Settings read-only while streaming No Targets and limits can change while flying; the governor adapts. Only mount-level settings (paths, FUSE) require unmounting. Flight report with a verdict Yes, extended Adds target fidelity per flight phase and what the governor learned.

docs.title: 3. AutoOrtho today: the problems this solves
docs.text:
• 148 keys, about 89 controls, 9 categories. There are two waiting systems side by side (maxwait / tile_time_budget / fallback_* and the [streaming] wait bands), 13 provider settings plus 3 legacy names, and about 12 worker and memory sizes.
  • Engine settings are frozen at startup. For example: live_builder_concurrency and background_builder_workers size thread pools once (getortho.py:8740), live_tile_admission creates a fixed BoundedSemaphore (getortho.py:1418), and prefetch radius and lookahead are read in the prefetcher constructor (getortho.py:5344). Only the broker's per-origin AIMD controller adapts at runtime.
  • No real resource checks. RAM and VRAM appear only in tooltip text ("every extra ZL increases VRAM … by 4x"). Nothing compares a chosen target with the machine. Because the texture size is 256 × chunks (_calc_required_buffer_size() switches to 8K at ZL17 bulk or ZL19 airports), one slider step can quietly quadruple graphics memory.
  • Profiles are fixed tables. The four "performance profiles" (ui/main_window.py:_apply_settings_preset) write UI widgets with values that suit nobody's PC in particular. For example, "Quality" sets tile_time_budget to 300 s.
  • The wizard does not ask what the user wants and measures nothing.
  • Settings are defined in four or five places: the _defaults string, two widget-name dictionaries, ui/config_validation.py, and the slider ranges.

docs.title: 4.1 Target: what the user wants
docs.text:
The existing keys stay, with the same meaning, so current configs keep working:

  • max_zoom_mode = fixed | dynamic
  • max_zoom, max_zoom_near_airports (fixed mode)
  • dynamic_zoom_steps (altitude → zoom and airport zoom)

What changes is how they are presented and checked:

  • Quality target page with two modes:
  • Fixed: two sliders (Scenery ZL, Airport ZL).
  • By altitude: the existing step editor and chart (ui/dynamic_zoom_editor.py), with its Airliner / General Aviation / Low VRAM presets.
  • Live cost preview under the target, recomputed on every change:
  • Graphics memory for photo textures near the aircraft, against this PC's card (from the paging model, the texture size per step and measured flight data).
  • Download per new 1° area, and the Mbit/s needed to keep up at a typical speed for that altitude step.
  • Disk per 1° area.
  • A traffic light for each, from the guards (§4.3).
  • Target presets are shortcuts, not modes. Picking "Airliner" fills the steps; the user can then edit them. A short "Not sure? Let AutoOrtho suggest a target" button uses the connection test plus detected hardware to fill in a target that should be reachable.
  • min_zoom moves to Expert. The low-zoom base already covers far scenery.

Target fidelity is the governor's goal, and the number shown to the user:

Target fidelity = the share of X-Plane's near-band reads (mips 0 to 1) answered at the target zoom within the wait budget, over the last N minutes.

Plus time to sharp: after a new area loads, how long until near reads are at the target.

docs.title: 4.2 Limits: what the user allows
docs.text:
New [limits] section. Every value defaults to auto (derived from the detected machine). The user can set a lower ceiling:

Limit auto means Governs ram_gb AutoOrtho may use up to about 25 % of physical RAM, and always leaves max(4 GB, 20 %) free for X-Plane and Windows memory cache, predictive memory, tile image cache, write buffers, build buffers vram_gb card memory minus an X-Plane reserve (about 5 GB, adjustable) the target's projected photo-texture memory; texture-size lever if allowed bandwidth_mbps unlimited (the governor finds the line's capacity) download concurrency ceiling, plus an optional token bucket so other apps keep some bandwidth cpu_cores physical cores minus 2, kept for X-Plane builder workers, native pipeline threads, background builds disk_cache_gb today's file_cache_size disk budget manager protect_sim_fps (optional) off if on, the governor backs off background work when X-Plane's frame time rises while AutoOrtho is busy (needs the sim/operation/misc/frame_rate_period dataref added to datareftrack.py)

Limits are hard ceilings for the governor. The governor never exceeds them, even if fidelity suffers. When a limit is the reason the target isn't reached, the UI says so ("Bandwidth limit 50 Mbit/s reached; target fidelity 81 %").

docs.title: 4.3 Guards: protection that warns but does not block
docs.text:
Today AutoOrtho has no RAM or VRAM checks beyond tooltip text, so these are new. They run in three places:

  1. When editing the target or limits. The cost preview turns amber or red, with a one-line reason and a Fix button. Fix offers the nearest target that fits (for example "lower airport ZL to 18"), or raises the relevant limit if headroom exists.
  2. VRAM: projected photo-texture memory for the highest step + X-Plane reserve > card → red.
  3. RAM: limits set above what the machine can spare → red.
  4. Disk: cache folder free space < cache limit + safety margin → amber.
  5. Bandwidth: measured capacity (connection test or learned profile) < what the target needs at that step's typical speed → amber ("expect blurry moments in new areas").
  6. At mount time. The same checks run once more and show a notice on Home if something changed (another drive, new card, very low free RAM).
  7. During the flight (emergency brakes). These act immediately, outside the governor's normal step rules:
  8. Free RAM below max(1.5 GB, 8 %) → pause prefetch, shrink caches to their minimum, drop background builds. Release gradually once RAM recovers.
  9. AutoOrtho's own memory above ram_gb → same.
  10. Disk free below the safety margin → stop writing new cache entries, keep serving.
  11. Each activation shows on the live panel and in the log, and is counted in the flight report.

docs.title: 4.4 Governor: how AutoOrtho gets there
docs.text: The governor runs in the parent process. It sees every mount worker's stats (through the existing aostats manager store), the broker, and system counters. It adjusts levers within the ranges allowed by the limits.

docs.title: Control loops
docs.text:
Loop Period Mechanism Owner Fast sub-second per-origin AIMD in the broker, priority queues, wait bands existing code, unchanged Medium 5 to 10 s bottleneck controller: find what is holding fidelity back, move one lever one step, check the result, keep or revert new Slow per flight and across flights learned profile: stores where the medium loop settled, the fitted paging k, measured graphics memory; warm-starts the next flight; tells the user when the target is consistently out of reach new

The medium loop sets the ceilings the fast loop works inside. For example, the governor raises the broker's per-origin maximum, and AIMD still ramps up to it response by response. The two loops do not fight.

docs.title: Signals (sampled every 2 s, smoothed)
docs.text:
• Fidelity and waits: near and middle reads served at target vs below target, stand-ins, wait-band timeouts, chunk_missing_count, upscaled_chunk_count, row_batch_deadline_expired.
  • Network: throughput, tile latency (p50/p90), error and timeout share per origin, broker queue depth and time spent queued.
  • Compute: builder utilisation, streaming_builder_queue_wait_count, tile-queue waits, AutoOrtho CPU %, system CPU %.
  • Memory: free RAM, AutoOrtho RSS (parent + workers), cache hit rates (tile_mem_hits / tile_mem_miss).
  • Flight context: phase (starting / taxi / climb / cruise / approach) from wait_bands.StartTracker, altitude, ground speed, current dynamic zoom step.
  • Optional: X-Plane frame time (see protect_sim_fps).

docs.title: Bottleneck classifier (rule table, evaluated each tick)
docs.text: State Signs Lever moved (one step) Network-bound, line has room broker queue full, no errors, tile latency stable, throughput under the measured line capacity and under bandwidth_mbps raise download concurrency ceiling Network-bound, line full / server pushing back errors or timeouts > 3 %, or latency rising with no throughput gain lower concurrency ceiling; reduce prefetch depth so live reads get the line Compute-bound chunks waiting in builder queues, builders 100 % busy, CPU under cpu_cores raise live builders (then background builders) Compute-bound at limit same, but CPU at limit, or sim frame time rising lower background builds, raise build interval; keep live builders Memory pressure free RAM falling toward the guard, or RSS near ram_gb shrink tile image cache, then predictive memory, then memory cache Wait-bound near reads time out, but the real chunk arrives soon after (p80 ≤ 12 s) raise band_max_wait_seconds (or near_wait_seconds while starting) Behind the aircraft near reads hit tiles that prefetch never queued, line and CPU have room extend prefetch lookahead and radius Headroom everywhere fidelity ≥ 98 % and resources well under limits slowly decay levers toward the baseline, to free resources for X-Plane Target unreachable every lever at its limit for N minutes, fidelity still low no lever left: degrade gracefully (below) and notify

docs.title: Rules that keep it stable
docs.text:
• One lever per tick. Hysteresis bands. A cooldown per lever (for example 30 s).
  • Keep or revert: after a change, compare fidelity and the bottleneck signal over the next window. If either is worse, revert and put that lever on a longer cooldown. This is a simple hill-climb with rollback, so the governor can't drift into a bad state.
  • Phase-aware step sizes: big steps while the flight is starting (getting to sharp scenery quickly matters most), small steps in cruise.
  • Pinned values are never touched. Hard limits are never exceeded.

docs.title: Graceful degradation when the target is out of reach
docs.text:
Applied in this order, each step shown on the live panel:

  1. Spend less on far work: shorter prefetch lookahead, smaller radius.
  2. Far and middle bands may use a zoom one level below target (mostly already true via the low-zoom base and wait bands; the governor makes it explicit and measured).
  3. Optional, if the user allowed it: cap texture size (shrink imagery above 4096 px instead of building 8K). Same zoom level, a quarter of the VRAM.
  4. Notify the user: "Your ZL18 target reached 72 % fidelity in cruise. The limit is your connection (about 60 Mbit/s). Options: lower the cruise step to ZL16 · raise the bandwidth limit · keep it".

The governor never silently lowers the user's target. Only the user changes the target.

docs.title: Learning across flights (the slow loop)
docs.text:
• At unmount, save the converged lever values, the measured line capacity, the fitted paging k and the measured graphics memory to ~/.autoortho-data/profile/learned.json, keyed by (target profile hash, imagery provider, network fingerprint such as gateway MAC or SSID hash).
  • The next flight with the same key starts from those values, so it is near-optimal from the first minute.
  • First ever flight: warm start from the connection test (concurrency) and the hardware baseline (workers and memory).
  • Reset learned settings on the Tuning page clears the profile.

docs.title: Modes
docs.text: Mode Behaviour Auto (default) Adjusts live, within limits, shows everything. Advise Computes the same decisions but only lists them on Home (OSXP style). Nothing changes without Apply. Off Fixed values from the registry and user settings, as today. For A/B testing and troubleshooting.

docs.title: 5. Transparency
docs.text: The governor must be easy to inspect. Users should be able to see what it is doing without reading the log.

docs.title: 5.1 Home: live tuning card (while mounted)
docs.text:
Quality target   ZL17 · airports ZL18 (By altitude: "General Aviation", step 0-5000 ft)
Delivering       96 % at target · sharp in 38 s after the last area load
Bottleneck       Network: 142 of ~160 Mbit/s       [Limits: RAM 6.1/8 GB · CPU 6/10 cores · VRAM ok]
Last change      +16 parallel downloads: queue was full, no errors (12 s ago)       [Details]

docs.title: 5.2 Tuning page
docs.text:
• Table: setting · current value · allowed range (from limits) · source (baseline / learned / governor / pinned) · last change and reason · pin toggle.
  • Timeline chart for the session: fidelity, throughput, CPU, RAM, with each governor decision marked. Click a marker to see the decision and what happened after.
  • Buttons: Mode (Auto / Advise / Off) · Reset learned settings · Export tuning report.

docs.title: 5.3 Log and report
docs.text:
• Every decision is logged on one line: Governor: raise provider ceiling 128→144 (network-bound: queue 100 %, errors 0.2 %, 142 Mbit/s); fidelity 91 %→?, followed by a kept or reverted line.
  • The flight report (existing diagnostics Markdown/JSON) gains:
  • a verdict line,
  • fidelity by phase,
  • guard activations,
  • what was learned for next time ("starts next flight at 144 parallel downloads, 10 live builders").

docs.title: 6.1 One registry
docs.text:
Replace the _defaults string, the widget-name dictionaries and the scattered ranges with one registry (autoortho/settings/registry.py):

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SettingSpec:
    key: str                 # "autoortho.live_builder_concurrency"
    type: type
    default: Any
    range: tuple | None      # absolute bounds; limits may narrow them
    tier: Tier               # ESSENTIAL | TUNING | EXPERT | INTERNAL | RETIRED
    owner: Owner             # TARGET | LIMIT | USER | GOVERNED | HARDWARE | FIXED
    live: bool               # can change without remount
    lever: LeverSpec | None  # for GOVERNED: step size, cooldown, which limit bounds it
    label: str
    help: str
    replaced_by: str | None

docs.title: 6.2 Layered resolution
docs.text:
From lowest to highest priority:

packaged default
  → hardware baseline     (cores, RAM, VRAM: computed at start)
  → learned profile       (from previous flights with the same target/provider/network)
  → governor live value   (in memory only, during the flight)
  → user pin              (explicit value: the governor never touches it)
clamped by limits         (hard ceiling for everything above, except pins, which the guards warn about)
= effective value + source + reason
  • The ini stores intent only: paths, target, limits, mode, look settings and pins. Values equal to their computed value are not written. A fresh file is about 25 lines instead of about 150.
  • Startup consumers do not change. The resolver runs inside AOConfig.load() and fills the same CFG.<section>.<key> attributes read today.
  • Live levers need the engine changes in §8.

docs.title: 6.3 UI tiers
docs.text: Tier Contents Essentials (about 15 controls) Quality target (Fixed / By altitude + presets + cost preview) · Limits (Auto, or custom sliders) · Governor mode · X-Plane / Scenery / Cache folders · Cache limit · Imagery source · Seasons on/off + strength · Night exclusion · Reduce sunrise shine · SimBrief ID + use flight plan · Hide window while running Tuning (live) The table, timeline and buttons from §5.2 Expert A searchable table of every registry key: effective value, default, source and help. Editing a value pins it. Home shows "3 pinned expert values · Review". The current category pages (DDS, pipeline, FUSE, provider, diagnostics) can stay as grouped views over the same registry during the transition.

docs.title: 6.4 Apply model
docs.text: Keep Apply/Revert. Targets, limits and mode are live=True: Apply takes effect immediately and the governor adapts. Mount-level keys (paths, FUSE, pipeline mode) show "Takes effect at next mount" and are disabled while mounted.

docs.title: 7. First-run wizard (six steps)
docs.text:
1. Welcome and checks: FUSE / WinFsp / macFUSE readiness (merges today's Dependencies page).
  2. X-Plane: auto-detect first, browse second.
  3. Scenery: install a region or point at existing packages.
  4. Cache: one folder, free space, a suggested cache limit. Long-term cache and download directory move to Expert.
  5. Quality target:
  6. Pick Fixed or By altitude, with presets.
  7. Test my connection (30 s, OSXP's method through AutoOrtho's broker). The cost preview turns green, amber or red for this PC.
  8. "Suggest a target for me" fills in a target that should be reachable.
  9. The test result also seeds the governor.
  10. Limits and ready: "Use what's available (recommended)" or set limits. Summary, plus "Start AutoOrtho now".

docs.title: 8. Engine work: making levers live
docs.text:
Most levers are read once today. Each needs a small, mechanical change so the governor can move it.

Lever Read today Change Download concurrency ceiling broker _adaptive_config at start broker accepts set_origin_ceiling() from the parent (same process; easy) Bandwidth cap none token bucket in the broker dispatcher live_builder_concurrency, background_builder_workers pool sizes at getortho.py:8740 create pools at the ceiling (the cpu_cores limit); gate them with a resizable semaphore whose permit count the governor sets live_tile_admission BoundedSemaphore at getortho.py:1418 same resizable gate prefetch_lookahead, prefetch_radius_nm, prefetch_max_chunks prefetcher constructor (getortho.py:5344) read through a LiveSettings accessor each cycle predictive_dds_memory_mb, tile_image_cache_mb, cache_mem_limit budgets at init budget objects with resize(); shrinking evicts down to the new size band_max_wait_seconds, near_wait_seconds, paging_k streaming_options (already read at call time) none Texture size cap (optional) none TexturePlan + downscale before encode + plan-keyed DDS cache (the largest item; can come last)

Parent → worker channel. Mount workers are separate processes (process_supervisor.py). Add a small governor/ key space to the existing aostats manager store (already shared and authenticated). The governor writes lever values there; each worker's LiveSettings polls it every 1 to 2 s. No new IPC mechanism is needed.

Wait consolidation. Before the governor can tune waits cleanly, the wait bands should be the only live-read policy. List every caller of _row_wait_seconds() / QualityDeadlinePolicy that still uses tile_time_budget / maxwait, move them to band budgets, then retire the legacy keys.

docs.title: 10. Migration
docs.text:
• Bump CONFIG_REVISION and extend _migrate_config_revision().
  • Target keys are kept as they are. Nobody's scenery changes after the update.
  • Engine keys equal to the old packaged defaults are dropped and become governed.
  • Engine keys that differ become pins. The governor respects them. Home shows "AutoOrtho now tunes engine settings automatically. 4 of your values were kept as pinned · Review", with Unpin all.
  • Old retired keys are migrated (_migrate_legacy_provider_options exists) and removed.
  • The four performance profiles are removed. Their intent is now covered by the target presets, the limits and the governor.

docs.title: 11. Rollout (each phase can ship on its own)
docs.text:
Phase Content Risk User benefit 1. Registry + resolver Registry generated from _defaults; resolver fills CFG; sparse writes; retire R keys; Expert table Low: consumers unchanged Smaller config, visible overrides 2. Hardware baseline + guards Detect cores/RAM/VRAM/disk; derive starting values; cost preview and guard checks on the target page; emergency RAM brake Low Protection from over-sized targets 3. Limits + connection test [limits]; port the connection test; wizard Quality and Limits steps Low Fast setup, safe ceilings 4. Live levers Resizable gates and budgets, LiveSettings, parent → worker channel Medium: touches pool creation Prerequisite for the governor 5. Governor in Advise mode Signals, classifier, decisions shown but not applied; live panel and timeline Low: changes nothing Validates decisions on real flights 6. Governor in Auto mode Applies decisions with keep/revert; learned profiles and warm start Medium Settings tune themselves 7. Wait consolidation Bands become the only live policy; retire legacy wait keys Medium Removes the most confusing group 8. Optional texture-size lever TexturePlan, downscale before encode, plan-keyed DDS cache Medium–high: native pipeline Higher zoom within VRAM limits 9. Home revamp (§13) State-based layout, HomeSnapshot from the sampler, notices, last-flight card. Can start after phase 2 with stats only; the fidelity hero and Auto-tuning block arrive with phases 5–6 Low: UI only Users see what AutoOrtho is doing and whether it keeps up

Shipping Advise before Auto lets us compare the governor's decisions with what experienced users would do, using real flight reports, before it changes anything.

docs.title: 12. Risks and open questions
docs.text:
• Oscillation and noise. Mitigated by one lever per tick, hysteresis, cooldowns, keep/revert, and smoothing over windows. Needs a replay harness: record signals from real flights (the diagnostics checkpoints already capture much of this) and run the governor offline against them in tests.
  • Interaction with AIMD. The governor only moves ceilings; AIMD keeps the per-response loop. Check that a lower ceiling never undercuts AIMD's floor (provider_origin_min_concurrency).
  • Latency of the cross-process channel. A 1 to 2 s poll is fine for the medium loop. Emergency brakes should run in each worker locally as well, not only in the parent.
  • Pinned values that break the target. The guards warn ("pinned live_builder_concurrency=2 is limiting fidelity"), but pins are respected.
  • VRAM accuracy on macOS and Linux. Unknown VRAM → no VRAM warnings and a conservative suggested target.
  • Network fingerprint privacy. Store only a salted hash, locally.
  • Frame-time protection needs a new dataref subscription. Verify how fast datareftrack updates and how noisy the value is before relying on it.
  • Restart semantics: confirm per key what a running mount can pick up live, and set SettingSpec.live accordingly.

docs.title: 13. Home (main menu) revamp
docs.text: The Target / Limits / Governor model needs a front page that shows it working. Today's Home can't do that.

docs.title: 13.1 What Home shows today
docs.text:
ui/pages/home_page.py shows ten cards of equal weight in a 2-column grid: Runtime, Readiness, X-Plane, Mounted Scenery, Provider, SimBrief, Cache, Task, Throughput, Recent Failure.

  • Nothing about streaming. Task and Throughput are filled from the scenery-package download task manager (_refresh_phase3_task_views), not from the streaming engine. While flying, Home shows no imagery speed, no quality, and no resource use.
  • Everything has the same weight. "SimBrief: No flight plan" takes as much space as "Runtime".
  • Cards stay up when they have nothing to say. For example "✓ No recent failures" and "○ Idle".
  • No sense of time. There are no trends, so you can't tell "slow right now" from "slow all flight".
  • The raw counters exist (aostats, the web templates/stats.html page), but they are engine counters (chunks, hits, queue skips), not answers.

docs.title: 13.2 Principles
docs.text:
1. Answer four questions, in this order:
  2. Is it working?
  3. Am I getting the quality I asked for?
  4. What is it using?
  5. Do I need to do anything?
  6. Every number must be actionable or reassuring. If a value would not change what the user understands or decides, it belongs on the Tuning or Diagnostics page, not on Home.
  7. The layout follows the state. Stopped, Starting, Flying and After flight each show what matters then. Cards don't sit around showing nothing useful.
  8. One headline, detail on demand. Each block has one number. Clicking it opens the detail (Tuning page, timeline, diagnostics report).
  9. Plain units. % sharp, Mbit/s, GB, minutes and nm. Never chunks, mipmaps, permits or queue depths.
  10. Calm updates. Numbers refresh at 1 Hz with smoothing; trend lines use 5 s buckets. Values freeze, labelled "paused", while X-Plane is paused. Nothing flickers.
